title: Garlic Bread
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F.
Mash the softened butter with the garlic and parsley and a pinch of salt.
Split the baguette lengthwise and spread the butter over both cut faces.
Bake on a sheet pan for 10 minutes, then broil for 2 more until the edges brown.
Cut into fingers and serve while the butter is still bubbling.

title: Spaghetti Aglio e Olio
steps: Boil the spaghetti in well-salted water until just short of al dente.
Meanwhile warm the olive oil in a skillet and cook the garlic gently until pale gold — do not let it brown.
Add the red pepper flakes and a ladle of pasta water to the skillet.
Drain the pasta and toss it in the skillet for a minute so the sauce clings.
Off the heat, stir through the parsley and serve.

title: Margherita Pizza
steps: Put the pizza stone in the oven and heat to its highest setting for a full hour.
Stretch the dough by hand to a thin round, leaving the rim a little thicker.
Spread a thin layer of crushed tomatoes, leaving the rim bare, and tear the mozzarella over it.
Slide onto the stone and bake 7-10 minutes until the crust is blistered.
Finish with torn basil and a drizzle of olive oil.

title: Caesar Salad
steps: Mash the garlic to a paste with a little salt.
Whisk the garlic with lemon juice, then whisk in the olive oil to make the dressing.
Tear the romaine into a bowl and toss with just enough dressing to coat.
Add the croutons and most of the parmesan, toss once more, and finish with the rest.

title: Tomato Soup
steps: Soften the onion in the olive oil over medium heat, then add the garlic for a minute.
Add the roughly chopped tomatoes and a cup of water, and simmer 25 minutes.
Blend until smooth, season, and stir in the basil at the last moment.

title: Roasted Vegetables
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F.
Cut everything to a similar size so it cooks evenly, and toss with the oil, rosemary, salt and pepper.
Spread on a sheet pan in a single layer — crowding steams instead of roasts.
Roast 35 minutes, turning once, until the edges are properly browned.

title: Spaghetti Carbonara
steps: Beat the eggs with the parmesan and a great deal of black pepper.
Render the pancetta slowly in a cold skillet until crisp; keep the fat.
Boil the spaghetti until al dente and reserve a mug of the water.
Off the heat, toss the drained pasta with the pancetta, then the egg mixture, loosening with pasta water until glossy.
The residual heat cooks the egg — if the pan is on the flame you will get scrambled egg instead of sauce.

title: Marinara Sauce
steps: Soften the onion in the olive oil over low heat for 10 minutes without colouring it.
Add the garlic and oregano and cook one minute more.
Pour in the tomatoes, season, and simmer uncovered for 30 minutes until it no longer tastes raw.
Tear in the basil off the heat. Keeps a week in the fridge and freezes well.

title: Beef Lasagna
steps: Brown the beef with the onion and garlic, add the tomatoes and simmer 30 minutes.
Beat the egg into the ricotta with the parmesan and season well.
Heat the oven to 375°F.
Layer sauce, noodles, ricotta and mozzarella twice over, finishing with sauce and cheese.
Cover with foil and bake 30 minutes, uncover and bake 20 more.
Rest 20 minutes before cutting or it will slump on the plate.

title: Mushroom Risotto
steps: Keep the stock at a bare simmer in a second pan.
Brown the mushrooms hard in a little butter and set aside — crowded mushrooms steam.
Soften the shallot, add the rice and toast 2 minutes until the grains look translucent at the edge.
Add the wine and let it cook away, then add stock a ladle at a time, stirring, for about 18 minutes.
Stir the mushrooms, remaining butter and parmesan through off the heat and let it rest 2 minutes.

title: Caprese Salad
steps: Slice the tomatoes and mozzarella about the same thickness.
Shingle them alternately on a plate, tucking basil leaves between.
Season with flaky salt, then dress with olive oil and balsamic just before serving.

title: Shrimp Scampi
steps: Boil the linguine in salted water.
Melt half the butter and cook the garlic and pepper flakes 30 seconds.
Add the shrimp in one layer and cook 90 seconds a side until just opaque, then lift them out.
Deglaze with the wine, reduce by half, then whisk in the rest of the butter and the lemon juice.
Return the shrimp, toss with the drained pasta and the parsley, and serve at once.

title: Chicken Tacos
steps: Toss the chicken with the seasoning and a little oil and let it sit while the pan heats.
Sear hard in a skillet 5-6 minutes a side, then rest and chop.
Warm the tortillas directly over a flame or in a dry pan until pliable and freckled.
Build with chicken, onion, cilantro, queso fresco and salsa, with lime to squeeze over.

title: Black Bean Soup
steps: Soften the onion, then add the garlic and spices and cook until fragrant.
Add the beans and stock and simmer 25 minutes.
Blend about half the pot so it thickens but keeps some texture.
Finish with plenty of lime juice — it is what makes the whole thing taste like something — and cilantro.

title: Slow Cooker Beef Barbacoa
steps: Blend the chipotles, garlic, cumin, oregano, lime juice and stock to a smooth sauce.
Cut the beef into large chunks, season, and brown them if you have time — it is worth it.
Put everything in the slow cooker with the bay leaves and cook on low for 8 hours.
Shred with two forks and let the meat sit in its juices before serving.

title: Guacamole
steps: Mash the avocado coarsely — it should stay lumpy.
Fold in the lime juice, onion, cilantro, jalapeño and salt.
Taste and add more lime and salt than feels right; avocado swallows both.

title: Chicken Fried Rice
steps: Day-old cold rice is not a suggestion — fresh rice turns to porridge in the wok.
Scramble the egg in a hot oiled wok, then remove it.
Stir-fry the chicken until cooked through, add the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds.
Add the rice and press it against the pan to fry rather than stir constantly.
Return the egg, add the peas, soy sauce and sesame oil, and toss through the green onions.

title: Beef and Broccoli Stir-Fry
steps: Toss the beef with a tablespoon of the cornstarch and a splash of soy sauce and leave 15 minutes.
Mix the rest of the soy sauce, oyster sauce and cornstarch with a quarter cup of water.
Sear the beef in a screaming-hot wok in two batches so it browns instead of stewing, and set aside.
Stir-fry the broccoli with a splash of water and a lid for 3 minutes until bright green.
Add the garlic and ginger, return the beef, pour in the sauce and toss until it thickens and coats. Serve over rice.

title: Shrimp Pad Thai
steps: Soak the rice noodles in warm water until pliable but still firm; they finish in the pan.
Stir the fish sauce, tamarind and sugar together — this is the whole sauce.
Fry the shrimp in a hot wok until pink and lift them out.
Scramble the eggs, add the drained noodles and the sauce, and toss until absorbed.
Return the shrimp, throw in the bean sprouts and green onions for 30 seconds, and serve with peanuts and lime.

title: Thai Green Curry with Chicken
steps: Fry the curry paste in the thick cream from the top of a coconut milk can until it splits and smells fragrant.
Add the chicken and turn it in the paste, then pour in the rest of the coconut milk and the lemongrass.
Simmer 15 minutes, add the peppers for the last 5.
Season with fish sauce, pull out the lemongrass, stir in the basil and serve over jasmine rice.

title: Miso Soup with Tofu
steps: Simmer the stock with the mushrooms for 10 minutes.
Slacken the miso with a ladle of hot stock in a small bowl, then stir it back in.
Add the tofu and warm through — do not boil once the miso is in, it dulls the flavour.
Scatter with green onion and serve.

title: Teriyaki Salmon
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F.
Simmer the soy sauce, honey, mirin, ginger and garlic until it coats a spoon.
Put the salmon in a baking dish, spoon over half the glaze, and bake 12-14 minutes.
Brush with the rest of the glaze and finish with sesame seeds and green onion.

title: Bibimbap
steps: Cook each vegetable separately and season it on its own — that separation is the point of the dish.
Brown the beef with soy sauce and a little sesame oil.
Fry the eggs so the yolks stay runny.
Arrange rice in bowls with the vegetables, beef and kimchi in wedges around the edge and the egg on top.
Serve gochujang alongside and let everyone mix their own.

title: Vietnamese Noodle Salad
steps: Cook the rice noodles, then rinse them under cold water so they stop cooking and stop sticking.
Whisk the fish sauce, lime juice, sugar and jalapeño with three tablespoons of water.
Toss the cool noodles with the vegetables and most of the herbs.
Dress just before eating and top with peanuts and the rest of the herbs.

title: Chicken Tikka Masala
steps: Marinate the chicken overnight in the yogurt with half the garam masala, the ginger and half the garlic.
Broil or sear the chicken in batches until charred at the edges — the char is the flavour, not the sauce.
Soften the onions, add the rest of the garlic and the spices, then the tomatoes, and cook down 15 minutes.
Stir in the cream, return the chicken, and simmer 10 minutes.
Finish with cilantro and serve with naan.

title: Chana Masala
steps: Cook the onions past soft to properly browned — 12 minutes, not 4.
Add the ginger, garlic and ground spices and fry a minute until they darken.
Add the tomatoes and cook until the oil separates out at the edges.
Add the chickpeas with a splash of water and simmer 15 minutes, crushing a few against the pan to thicken it.
Finish with lemon juice and cilantro.

title: Red Lentil Dal
steps: Simmer the lentils in four cups of water with the turmeric for 20 minutes until collapsing.
Separately fry the onion, then the garlic, ginger and cumin, until deeply fragrant.
Stir that into the lentils with the coconut milk and simmer 10 minutes.
Wilt in the spinach and finish with lemon.

title: Hummus from Dried Chickpeas
steps: Soak the dried chickpeas overnight in plenty of cold water.
Drain, then boil with the baking soda for about an hour until they are falling apart — undercooked chickpeas make gritty hummus.
Blend the hot chickpeas with the tahini, lemon juice, garlic and cumin.
Let the processor run a full three minutes, adding ice water until it is pale and completely smooth.
Spread in a bowl and pool olive oil on top.

title: Greek Salad
steps: Cut the cucumber and tomatoes into large rough chunks, not neat dice.
Combine with the onion and olives, dress with oil, vinegar, oregano and salt.
Lay the feta on top in a slab rather than crumbling it, and let it sit ten minutes before serving.

title: Shakshuka
steps: Soften the peppers and onion in a cast iron skillet for 10 minutes.
Add the garlic, cumin, paprika and harissa, then the tomatoes, and simmer until thick.
Make wells in the sauce and crack an egg into each.
Cover and cook 6-8 minutes until the whites are set but the yolks still run.
Crumble over the feta, scatter cilantro, and serve from the pan with bread.

title: Grilled Lamb Kofta Skewers
steps: Soak wooden skewers in water so they do not burn on the grill.
Squeeze the liquid out of the grated onion, then mix everything but the pita and yogurt.
Knead the mixture a minute so it becomes tacky — that is what keeps it on the skewer.
Mould around the skewers and chill 20 minutes.
Grill over high heat 3-4 minutes a side. Serve in warm pita with yogurt.

title: Moroccan Chicken Tagine
steps: Brown the chicken skin-side down in a dutch oven and set aside.
Soften the onions in the fat, add the garlic and spices, and cook until fragrant.
Return the chicken with the stock and apricots, cover, and braise 45 minutes at a bare simmer.
Add the olives for the last 10 minutes.
Steam the couscous, fork it through, and serve the tagine over it with cilantro.

title: French Onion Soup
steps: Cook the onions in butter over medium-low heat for a full 45 minutes until mahogany. There is no shortcut here.
Deglaze with the wine and reduce almost to nothing.
Add the stock, thyme and bay and simmer 20 minutes.
Ladle into oven-safe bowls, float a slice of toasted baguette on each, and pile on the cheese.
Broil until the cheese is bubbling and browned in patches.

title: Ratatouille
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F.
Cook each vegetable separately in olive oil until browned, then combine — cooking them together gives you stew.
Layer into a baking dish with the tomatoes, garlic and thyme.
Bake 35 minutes until everything has collapsed together.
Tear over the basil. Better the next day.

title: Quiche Lorraine
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F and line a pie dish with the pastry.
Blind-bake the shell 15 minutes so the base does not go soggy.
Render the bacon, soften the onion in the fat, and scatter both over the shell with the cheese.
Beat the eggs with the cream and nutmeg, season, and pour in.
Bake 30-35 minutes until barely set with a slight wobble at the centre. Rest before slicing.

title: Buttermilk Pancakes
steps: Whisk the dry ingredients in one bowl and the wet in another.
Combine with a few strokes only — lumps are fine, a smooth batter makes tough pancakes.
Rest the batter 10 minutes while the griddle heats.
Cook until bubbles form and the edges look dry, then flip once.
Serve with maple syrup.

title: Chocolate Chip Cookies
steps: Set the butter out an hour ahead — properly softened butter is what makes the dough cream.
Beat the butter with both sugars for a full three minutes until pale.
Beat in the eggs one at a time, then the vanilla.
Fold in the flour, soda and salt, then the chocolate chips.
Chill the dough at least an hour, then bake at 375°F for 10-12 minutes; pull them while the centres still look underdone.

title: Beef Chili
steps: Brown the beef hard in a dutch oven and drain off most of the fat.
Add the onion and pepper and cook until soft, then the garlic and spices for a minute.
Add the tomatoes, beans and stock and simmer uncovered at least 90 minutes.
Season late — it concentrates as it reduces. Serve with cheddar.

title: Baked Macaroni and Cheese
steps: Boil the macaroni two minutes short of the packet time — it keeps cooking in the oven.
Make a roux with the butter and flour, then whisk in the warm milk and cook until it coats a spoon.
Off the heat, stir in most of the cheese and the mustard. Adding cheese off the heat is what stops it splitting.
Fold in the pasta, tip into a dish, and top with the rest of the cheese and the breadcrumbs.
Bake at 375°F for 25 minutes until browned and bubbling.

title: Buttermilk Fried Chicken
steps: Marinate the chicken in the seasoned buttermilk overnight.
Season the flour heavily — this is where the crust gets its flavour.
Dredge each piece, pressing the flour on, and rest 15 minutes so the coating hydrates and sticks.
Fry at 325°F, a few pieces at a time, 12-15 minutes; the oil must not crowd or the temperature crashes.
Drain on a rack, never on paper, so the underside stays crisp. Internal temperature should read 165°F.

title: Smoked Pulled Pork
steps: Rub the pork all over with the sugar, spices and salt and leave it overnight.
Light the smoker and hold it at 250°F.
Smoke fat-side up for about 6 hours until the bark is dark and the internal temperature hits 165°F.
Wrap in foil and continue to 203°F — another 4 hours or so. The stall is normal; wait it out.
Rest an hour wrapped, then pull with two forks and dress with barbecue sauce. Serve on buns.

title: Grilled Cheeseburgers
steps: Light the grill and get it properly hot.
Form patties wider than the bun with a dimple in the centre so they do not dome.
Salt only the outside, only just before grilling — salt mixed into the meat makes it springy.
Grill 3 minutes a side, adding cheese for the last minute under a cover.
Toast the buns on the grill and build.

title: New England Clam Chowder
steps: Render the bacon, remove it, and cook the onion and celery in the fat.
Stir in the butter and flour and cook the raw taste out for two minutes.
Add the clam juice and potatoes and simmer until the potatoes are tender.
Add the cream, clams, thyme and bay and warm through without boiling.
Scatter the bacon back over each bowl.

title: Sous Vide Steak
steps: Set the water bath to 130°F for medium-rare and let it come up to temperature.
Season the steaks, bag them with the herbs, and cook for 2 hours.
Take them out and dry the surface completely — a wet steak steams instead of searing.
Sear 45 seconds a side in a ripping-hot cast iron pan, basting with the butter and garlic.
Rest 5 minutes and slice against the grain.

title: Pressure Cooker Beef Stew
steps: Toss the beef in the flour and brown it in batches using the sauté function.
Cook the onion and celery, stir in the tomato paste, and deglaze with the wine.
Return the beef with the stock, thyme and bay. Pressure cook 35 minutes.
Release, add the carrots and potatoes, and cook a further 5 minutes under pressure.
Let the pressure fall naturally so the meat does not seize.

title: Roast Chicken with Root Vegetables
steps: Salt the chicken all over and leave it uncovered in the fridge overnight for the crispest skin.
Heat the oven to 425°F.
Work the softened butter and herbs under the breast skin, and put the lemon and garlic in the cavity.
Sit the bird on the vegetables in a roasting pan so they cook in the drippings.
Roast about 75 minutes until the thigh reads 165°F, then rest 20 minutes before carving.

title: Overnight Oats
steps: Stir the oats, milk, yogurt, chia and honey together in a jar.
Refrigerate overnight — the chia is what sets it rather than leaving it soupy.
Top with blueberries and sliced banana in the morning.

title: Avocado Toast with Egg
steps: Toast the sourdough hard — it has to hold the weight.
Mash the avocado with lemon juice and plenty of salt.
Fry the eggs to your liking.
Spread, top with an egg each, and finish with pepper flakes and flaky salt.

title: Banana Bread
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F and butter a loaf pan.
Cream the softened butter with the sugar, then beat in the eggs and vanilla.
Mash the bananas — the blacker the better — and stir them in.
Fold in the flour, soda and walnuts until only just combined.
Bake 60 minutes until a skewer comes out clean, and cool in the tin 10 minutes.

title: Butternut Squash Soup
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Halve the squash, oil it, and roast cut-side down 40 minutes.
Roasting rather than boiling the squash is most of the flavour — do not skip it.
Soften the onion, garlic, ginger and cumin in a stockpot.
Scoop in the squash flesh, add the stock, and simmer 15 minutes.
Blend smooth, stir in the coconut milk, and season.

title: Quinoa and Kale Salad
steps: Rinse the quinoa well, then cook in twice its volume of water for 15 minutes and cool.
Strip the kale from its stems, shred it, and massage with a little oil and salt until it darkens and softens.
Whisk the remaining oil with lemon juice and mustard.
Toss everything together and crumble the goat cheese over.

title: Spanish Tortilla
steps: Poach the potatoes and onion gently in the olive oil over low heat for 20 minutes until tender but not coloured.
Drain, reserving the oil, and fold the hot potatoes into the beaten eggs. Let it stand 10 minutes.
Cook in a skillet with a little of the reserved oil over medium-low heat until the base is set.
Slide onto a plate, invert back into the pan, and cook the other side.
The centre should stay just barely soft. Serve at room temperature.

title: Fish and Chips
steps: Cut the potatoes into thick chips and fry once at 300°F until soft but pale, then drain.
Whisk the flour with the wine to a thick batter and let it sit; keep it cold.
Raise the oil to 375°F and fry the chips again until golden — the second fry is what makes them crisp.
Dip the cod in the batter and fry 5-6 minutes until deep gold.
Serve with lemon and peas crushed with butter and salt.

title: Shepherd's Pie
steps: Boil the potatoes, then mash with the butter and milk and season hard.
Brown the lamb, add the onion and carrot, and cook until soft.
Stir in the tomato paste and Worcestershire, add the stock, and simmer until thickened.
Stir the peas through, tip into a baking dish, and spread the mash over, roughing up the top with a fork.
Bake at 400°F for 25 minutes until the peaks are browned.

title: Crispy Tofu and Vegetable Stir-Fry
steps: Press the tofu at least 20 minutes, then cube it and toss in cornstarch.
Fry the tofu in a hot wok without moving it until each face is crisp, then remove.
Stir-fry the harder vegetables first, then the bok choy leaves and snap peas.
Add the garlic and ginger, then the soy and hoisin with a splash of water.
Return the tofu, toss once, and serve over brown rice so it stays crisp.

title: Sheet Pan Sausage and Peppers
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F.
Give the potatoes a 15-minute head start on the pan — they take longer than everything else.
Add the sausage, peppers, onion and garlic, tossed with oil and seasoning.
Roast 25 minutes more, turning once, until the sausages are browned and the peppers are collapsing.

title: Chicken Noodle Soup
steps: Soften the onion, carrot and celery, then add the garlic, thyme and bay.
Add the stock and the chicken and simmer 25 minutes until the chicken shreds easily.
Lift the chicken out, shred it, and return it.
Cook the noodles separately and add them to each bowl — noodles cooked in the pot go to mush by the next day.
Finish with parsley.
